headline: Pretrained and conditioned models guide DNA, RNA, protein, and antibody design
label: Pretrained Conditioned Biomolecular Models
summary: Pretrained RNA, protein, and antibody priors are being paired with explicit conditioning for design and prediction tasks across recent preprints and papers.
synthesis: The common thread is conditioning biomolecular models on explicit variables, with pretrained or learned priors supplying biological structure. LOCOGEN reformulates diffusion guidance for regulatory DNA design as a locality problem, damping out-of-distribution guidance while protecting learned motif positions. iGC learns a somatic hypermutation prior from B-cell lineage trees and optimizes antibody binding through reinforcement learning with a KL constraint. LIMBER, a hybrid self-attention and Mamba RNA foundation model pretrained on 40.5M ncRNA sequences, targets RNA structure and function. Ernie-Switcher applies the RNAErnie foundation model to toehold switch design, reporting up to 35-fold ON/OFF ratios, while PRIDA couples pretrained protein and RNA language models with conditional domain-adversarial learning. What is new across these items is that the conditioning variable or constraint is made explicit, whether as a locality term, a KL penalty, or a domain condition. The items are heterogeneous: LOCOGEN, iGC, and ProteoCraft are design methods, whereas PRIDA and LIMBER address prediction and interpretation.
